title: Pesticides in our food: is organic worth it? | Nick Mole from PAN UK
summary: Podcast interview with a UK pesticide-campaign director arguing organic is the way to avoid residues and better for nature, that pesticides including glyphosate harm health, that mixtures are under-assessed, and that washing does little.

assertions.quote: if you want to avoid pesticide residues organic is definitely the way to go there's no no question about it

verdicts.note: USDA and EU residue monitoring and meta-analyses consistently find residues less frequent and lower on organic produce, though not absent.

assertions.quote: but whether it's it'll get rid of pesticides probably not

verdicts.note: Rinsing and baking-soda soaks remove part of surface residues, but systemic and absorbed residues stay in the produce.

assertions.quote: there are a very limited number of uh pesticides that that are allowed to be used in in organic

verdicts.note: The USDA National List and EU rules permit a set of natural and some synthetic pesticides in organic farming.

assertions.quote: they switched them to an organic diet for a month and I tested them again and there was a massive reduction

verdicts.note: Diet-switch studies in children and families show urinary pesticide metabolites fall sharply within days of eating organic.

assertions.quote: those who do have glyphosate in the urine have uh increased biomarkers for a range of cancers

verdicts.note: IARC's probable-carcinogen rating rests mainly on high occupational exposure; EPA and EFSA find dietary residue levels pose no meaningful risk, though evidence is contested.

assertions.quote: it's better for biodiversity it's better for you know the the water that comes off it

verdicts.note: Meta-analyses find roughly a third more species richness on organic farms on average, varying by taxon and landscape.

assertions.quote: I think you probably could put your trust in that kind of thing

verdicts.note: The largest documented organic fraud cases involved imported grain, though imports must meet the same rules and enforcement tightened under the 2023 SOE rule.

assertions.quote: pesticides are risk assessed individually ah okay okay so they're looked at individually and they're approved individually for use

verdicts.note: Approvals are mostly per active substance; EFSA and EPA run cumulative assessments for some chemical groups, but mixture effects remain little studied.
High occupational exposure to some pesticides is linked to cancers such as non-Hodgkin lymphoma, but evidence at dietary exposure levels is weak.

assertions.quote: it's much stronger on Animal Welfare than than a lot of certainly the Intensive um Factory farmed um Livestock systems

verdicts.note: Organic rules mandate outdoor access, pasture for ruminants and bans on some confinement practices, though they are weaker than dedicated welfare certifications.

assertions.quote: organic is not just marketing or hype actually has benefits absolutely it does yes

verdicts.note: The organic label is a legally enforced production standard with inspections and real input restrictions, even though it is heavily marketed.

assertions.quote: most people will probably glyphosate in their urine

verdicts.note: CDC biomonitoring detected glyphosate in roughly four in five US urine samples; detection says nothing about harm by itself.
